payload.title: Bag-out stops or stays in request with suspected AGV pair or robot sequence issue
payload.user_facing_summary: Use this flow when the site reports bag-out will not complete normally, is stuck in request, or manual bag-out is underway and support suspects an AGV, exchange pair, or robot sequencing problem.
payload.playbook_goal: Determine whether a bag-out stoppage is associated with AGV pair, robot sequence, or stuck-task conditions and guide supported recovery and validation.
observed_entry_symptoms: System stopped at bag-out after sorting
Bag-out entered request state and did not complete normally
Site is manually bagging out
Site suspects one of the exchange pairs
A robot or AGV may be out of sequence or stuck on task
An AGV is reported as not moving for an extended period

linked_runbooks.title: Recover an AGV That Lost a Tote Without an AGV Fault
linked_runbooks.summary: Restore the AGV and the missing tote to the system after an AGV loses a tote without the AGV itself faulting. The source sequence stops RMS, manually releases and moves the AGV to the Hospital, removes and re-adds the AGV at the Hospital station PC, power-cycles the AGV, repositions it at the Inbound Hospital Station QR code after its lights turn green, then removes and re-adds the missing tote.
linked_runbooks.when_to_use: Use when the AGV LOST TOTE NO FAULT recovery scenario applies and the AGV has lost a tote without the AGV itself faulting, using the recovery sequence documented in section 5.8.2.6.
not_for: Do not use for AGV fault scenarios not identified as "AGV LOST TOTE NO FAULT".
Do not use if the referenced Add/Remove AGV, Remove Tote, or Add Tote procedures cannot be completed.

payload.title: Clustered WCS web-application errors during robotic outage
payload.user_facing_summary: Use this candidate when support enters from application-side evidence such as clustered WCSWebApplication errors, Windows Error Reporting entries, or failed database-command events in Event Viewer during a robotic outage. The troubleshooting shape is to confirm the application fault pattern, assess whether it remains active after primary recovery, and escalate with the right evidence if the issue is unresolved or outside supported recovery scope.
payload.playbook_goal: Assess and contain a WCS web-application fault pattern that may accompany or outlast a robotic stoppage, and determine whether separate application or infrastructure escalation is required.

Application log shows Windows Error Reporting or Application Error entries around the outage time
Event Viewer shows failed database-command execution for WCSWebApplication
Support observes a faulted web application or webservice during or after robotic recovery
